rubrics.criterion: The main SFC entry (src/index.ts) no longer concentrates SFC compilation in one class-or-scope: the work is redistributed so that no remaining single class or single module still combines descriptor parsing/caching, language-block selection, script resolution, per-block proxy-module code generation, CSS-modules emission, hot-reload emission, and compiler-error formatting.
rubrics.rationale: This is the defining outcome of the instance: the maintainer observation is one class implementing many responsibilities that change for different reasons; a solution that leaves them together has not solved the reported problem regardless of how clean the result lies.

rubrics.criterion: Descriptor parsing and its per-file descriptor cache now live in a dedicated cohesive owner (own module or equivalent unit), and that owner is the single addressable place for reading/writing descriptors from both the main request flow and other in-package consumers; the entry does not hold its own duplicate cache.
rubrics.rationale: The descriptor cache is the process-wide state the injected class absorbed from the former descriptor-cache module and exported to peers; separating it back into an owner that serves every consumer is a distinct, independently checkable responsibility outcome.

rubrics.criterion: Script resolution — compileScript invocation and option mapping, the client/server resolved-script caches, the inline-template decision, and the imported-type dependency recording — has a dedicated cohesive owner separate from the request-flow entry, so template resolution and cache behavior can be changed without touching request code generation.
rubrics.rationale: Script resolution was the largest absorbed module in the injected diff (the deleted resolveScript owner) and carries the caches the webpack plugins watch; extracting it intact is a materially different obligation from descriptor caching or codegen.

rubrics.criterion: Language-block selection dispatch (?type=script|template|style|custom requests leaving through the block-loader callback) is implemented in a unit dedicated to block selection rather than as an embedded member of a general-purpose request class next to the generation code.
rubrics.rationale: The injected change folded the former selection module into the coordinator as one more method; re-establishing selection as its own concern is one of the independent accounting points for whether the class's responsibilities were actually redistributed.

rubrics.criterion: The code that constructs proxy-module imports and block requests (script/template/style/custom import statements, query stringification, attrs-to-query handling, inline-match-resource vs plain request routing) lives in codegen-oriented units separated from descriptor state ownership and from CSS-modules/hot-reload emission.
rubrics.rationale: Request-construction logic is the part of the god class that changes with webpack (query shape, match-resource experiments) rather than with Vue compiler behavior; it is a separate responsibility with its own failure modes, and the instance's prompt calls it out as the entry's core remaining job.

rubrics.criterion: CSS-modules emission (the cssModules object wiring exported per style module attribute, with the hot-reload rerender branch) is owned by a dedicated codegen unit rather than being inlined in the same scope as request construction or descriptor caching.
rubrics.rationale: The injected diff absorbed the dedicated CSS-modules codegen module into the class; restoring it as an independently owned concern is a distinct extraction the solver must localize by reading the style-import loop.

rubrics.criterion: Hot-reload code emission (client registration, template rerender acceptance callback, style rerender) is owned by a dedicated codegen unit with its own seams, not a private method cluster of a class that also owns parsing, caching and request construction.
rubrics.rationale: Hot-reload codegen was its own module before the modeled consolidation and is the responsibility the maintainer report explicitly tried to fix; knowing it was relocated is independently verifiable and instance-specific.

rubrics.criterion: Compiler-error code-frame formatting lives in its own unit (used mutually by the main flow and template compilation), not as a static method of the coordinator class that everything else also lives in.
rubrics.rationale: Error formatting is a diagnostics concern shared by two loaders; after the repair it should again be reachable without importing the main request machinery. It is the smallest of the extractions and a sound broader owner may legitimately absorb it, so it is nice_to_have rather than must_have.

rubrics.criterion: The coordinator class was not merely reshuffled: a single class that still declares most of the phase methods for the whole request flow and still owns the shared caches (e.g., a renamed/re-capitalized version of the injected class with the same method inventory minus a couple of moved helpers, or a class that statically exposes the descriptor/script caches to peers) makes this item fail.
rubrics.rationale: Renaming the class, splitting only one or two trivial helpers out, or moving the caches out while leaving all responsibilities in the same class are the cheapest evasive rewrites this instance specifically invites; the task is unsolved when they still hold.

rubrics.criterion: src/templateLoader.ts obtains the descriptor, the resolved script, and error formatting from the newly established owner units in normal imports — it no longer reaches them through the main entry's class, and its own compilation logic is unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The template loader is one of the three consumers the injected diff rewired toward the hub; re-pointing it at the new owners without altering its behavior is the accompanying change that makes the split real, and it is separately locatable.

rubrics.criterion: Both webpack plugin variants (src/pluginWebpack4.ts and src/pluginWebpack5.ts) reach the shared invalidation state (imported-type dependency map, descriptor cache, resolved-script caches) through its new owning unit, and their rule-rewriting and watch logic is otherwise untouched.
rubrics.rationale: The plugins were rewired onto the class in the injected diff; their rebuild/invalidation hooks are the only consumers that mutate the shared caches from outside the loader flow, so the ownership move must land there too or distinct caches silently diverge.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not rewrite consumers beyond the endpoint rewire the ownership move requires: the plugin variants' rule-cloning/condition logic and the pitcher or style loaders' internals are not restructured, merged into the entry, or re-authored around new abstractions.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible over-reach failure mode for this instance is 'fixing' the webpack 4/5 plugin internals while wires are hot, which inflates the diff review burden and multiplies behavioral risk in a refactor that was supposed to be a pure regression-free redistribution.

rubrics.criterion: No responsibility is left duplicated: the removed pieces (descriptor caching, script resolution, block selection, CSS-modules/HMR emission, error formatting) do not still exist as unused or shadowed copies inside the coordinator class alongside the new owners (e.g., a private static method or cache field that nothing references, or an old path still reachable in dead branches).
rubrics.rationale: Copy-out instead of move-out is the most likely artifact residue in a large-class split: leftover members of the injected class are exactly what a verifier can spot mechanically, and they mislead future maintainers about where work happens.

rubrics.criterion: The main entry does not retain a vestigial class shell: whatever remains in src/index.ts does not keep the injected coordinator's per-request field block, static state fields, or forwarding wrappers that only delegate to the new owners without adding request-flow meaning.
rubrics.rationale: Leaving the old class in place as a passthrough 'for compatibility' (nothing external ever required it — only in-package consumers did, and they were rewired) is a concrete residue this instance predicts.

rubrics.criterion: The shared caches exist exactly once with their consumers correctly pointed at that single instance — no leftover second declaration of the descriptor cache/script caches in the entry class alongside the owning unit's version (a state copy that would break identity semantics even if emission still looks right).
rubrics.rationale: Two live copies of a module-wide cache is the specific failure mode that turns an artifact hygiene problem into a latent behavioral bug (main request writing one cache while the template loader reads another); it is both instance-specific and mechanically checkable.

rubrics.criterion: The emitted proxy module is preserved: same import statements in the same order for template, script, styles and custom blocks, same ?vue&type=... query construction (id, index, scoped, ts, lang, src, external, blockType, issuerPath params), same export-helper attachment and runtime props (__scopeId, __file, __cssModules), and same custom-element mode output (per-block _style_N imports and XML wiring).
rubrics.rationale: The loader's observable product is the emitted module text, which webpack downstream tools snapshot and parse; a redistribution that alters emission is a behavior change, and the repo's own suite asserts heavily on emitted fragments.

rubrics.criterion: Descriptor identity semantics survive: the main request, block/template paths and subsequent rebuilds share the same parsed descriptor per file for a given compilerOptions (no double parsing to different instances), and the disk fallback for an uncached file (sub-loader/thread scenario) still works.
rubrics.rationale: Cache identity across loader invocations is the behavioral reason the descriptor cache exists; splitting state ownership is precisely where identity regressions appear while the tests still pass for single-file flows.

rubrics.criterion: Script resolution behavior is unchanged: compiled scripts are cached per descriptor identity (WeakMap semantics) with the existing client-vs-server split, canInlineTemplate makes the same inlining decision per mode, and resolveTemplateTSOptions handling for TS templates is preserved.
rubrics.rationale: The resolver is the hottest shared state in the package; per-descriptor caching and the client/server distinction are what keep HMR and SSR correct, and they are invisible to emitted-code assertions.

rubrics.criterion: The plugins' invalidation pass still works end-to-end: during script resolution the imported-type dependencies are still recorded against affected component files, and on rebuild/watch the plugins can still enumerate affected components, drop their resolved scripts from cache, and collect the descriptors needing recompilation in both webpack 4 and webpack 5 variants.
rubrics.rationale: The type-dependency bookkeeping spans three modules by design (resolution records, plugins consume); splitting ownership is where the wiring most easily ends at a state object the plugins no longer observe, which the default test suite does not exercise weld-for-weld.

rubrics.criterion: The missing-plugin error keeps its once-per-process semantics: it is still emitted on requests when VueLoaderPlugin is absent, thread-loader usage still short-circuits the check, and it does not become once-per-request (nor once-per-object) or move to first import.
rubrics.rationale: The warning flag was a process-wide boolean before the consolidation and got re-spelled as a static field; a refactor into per-request state (or per-module closure) silently changes how noisy webpack builds are, and no test asserts the spam rate.

rubrics.criterion: Language-block requests still return early through the block-loader callback: a ?type=... request selects the block via the loader callback and produces no proxy module (no main-module emission, no hanging promise), exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: In the injected shape the dispatch was a method returning undefined alongside generation code paths; a control-flow refactor that loses the early return breaks block loading outright and is the most likely structural regression of the control-flow move.

rubrics.criterion: One stable module id is used per component across all its block requests: the scope/id derivation (production source-dependent hashing vs development path-only id) runs once per component and is shared by the script import, the template query (?id=), scoped-style queries and the hot-reload registration, so blocks stay associated with their component (no re-derived per-block ids).
rubrics.rationale: The id was computed in the old flow once and consumed by four places; splitting code writers makes it easy to re-derive per block, which surfaces as broken scoped CSS/HMR association rather than test failures.

rubrics.criterion: The main loader's public contract is untouched: default export still calls like a webpack loader with the same signature, VueLoaderPlugin is still exported from the entry (and still dispatched by webpack version as before), and the VueLoaderOptions surface is unchanged for the many downstream consumers and tests.
rubrics.rationale: The entry is a package boundary; the maintainer report asks for an internal redistribution only. Contract drift here is how an internal refactor silently becomes a breaking release, and it is independently checkable from the diff.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leak request-scoped state into the shared units: the new owners do not gain module-level mutable per-request state (e.g., caches or flags that capture one request's loaderContext/filename and get read by the next request), which would serialize requests and corrupt concurrent builds.
rubrics.rationale: Splitting a class that held per-request instance fields invites fixing signatures by hoisting values to module scope — the same category of mistake the consolidation made in the other direction, and it is specific to this loader's multi-request lifetime.
